note: Honest list of what the corpus does not contain. status: not-found-in-permissive-source, sourceable-not-added, likely-copyrighted, out-of-scope-this-round. "sourceable-not-added" means a permissive source was seen but not fetched or used this round. Nothing in the registry is typed from memory (typedFromMemory is false everywhere).

audit.note: avot-1 was cut before its closing clause because of a scrambled divine name in the source; avot-closing now supplies it from Metsudah.
Modim and the middle blessings are gaps.
Wine blessing is shared with Kiddush.

audit.item: Torah service: blessings before and after the aliyah

audit.note: Echad Eloheinu and Av harachamim are gaps.
The composite "Adonai melech" line is a gap (g-ein-kamocha-composite).
Rest of Psalm 145 is a gap.
Opening words only. Full texts and matriarch versions are gaps.

gaps.name: Echad Eloheinu gadol adoneinu kadosh venora shemo
gaps.whereInService: Torah service, after the Shema line
gaps.why: The only pointed text found was the Daat Siddur Ashkenaz version on Sefaria, whose pointing is defective (omits holam on vav, uses abbreviations for the divine name). Not typed from memory.

gaps.name: Adonai melech, Adonai malach, Adonai yimloch le-olam va-ed (middle of Ein Kamocha)
gaps.why: Same reason as above (Daat text only). The verse lines before and after it are in the registry.

gaps.name: Av harachamim heitiva (after Ein Kamocha)

gaps.name: Ein Keloheinu
gaps.why: Only the defective Daat text found; the Metsudah weekday leaf does not exist.

gaps.name: Full Mi sheberach texts (for an aliyah, for the sick, for a birth, for a bar/bat mitzvah)
gaps.why: Sefard Torat Emet (Public Domain label) has the Orthodox texts, but they contain name placeholders and holiday variants in parentheses that need design decisions; matriarch versions used by Reform and Conservative congregations were not found in an open source.
